messages:
maya: quick flag — surge in token load from a single tenant in us-west-2, GPU pools creeping to 92% util. queue length up ~1200.
ben: yea saw that, mostly long-context chat sessions. batching helps but the KV cache churn is killing us.
carla: any calc on how that maps to our TPM/RPM guardrails? we need a fast way to set per-tenant throttles without manual guessing.
maya: rough back-of-envelope: avg request 3.2k tokens, avg latency 210ms per token on A100-40 (including batching variance). so per-GPU token throughput ~= (1 / 0.21) * 1 = ~4.7 tokens/sec? that seems off.
ben: that number is mixed units. better to do capacity in tokens/sec: measured steady-state decode = 250 tokens/sec per GPU for this model at our current kernel set.
ben: so a pool of 16 GPUs -> 4000 tokens/sec -> 240k tokens/min -> 14.4M tokens/hour.
carla: okay, translate to RPM (requests/min): if avg request is 3200 tokens -> RPM = tokens/min / avg_tokens = 240k / 3200 = 75 rpm for that pool.
carla: that's per pool capacity; for multi-tenant we want per-tenant soft limit = pool_capacity * share_pct. e.g., 20% -> 15 rpm or ~48 tpm.
maya: want to codify this to compute conservative TPM using p95 request size. propose formula in ops docs:
    ```
    pool_tokens_per_sec = GPUs_in_pool * tokens_per_sec_per_GPU
    pool_tpm = pool_tokens_per_sec * 60
    tenant_tpm = floor(pool_tpm * tenant_share)
    tenant_rpm = floor(tenant_tpm / p95_tokens_per_request)
    ```
raj: +1. Can we also account for KV cache hit rate? effective token/sec increases when cache hit rate high.
raj: suggestion: adjust tokens_per_sec_per_GPU = baseline_decode * (1 + cache_hit_multiplier * (hit_rate - baseline_hit)). baseline_hit = 0.25, cache_hit_multiplier ~0.4 (empirical)
ben: also need headroom for spikes and network jitter. multiply pool_tpm by 0.8 for operational headroom.
carla: so final tenant_tpm = floor(pool_tpm * 0.8 * tenant_share). good.
maya: for rollout: I'll push a quick script to compute tenant limits and generate quota objects. sample cc:
    ```json
    {
      "pool_id": "us-west-2-a",
      "gpus": 16,
      "tokens_per_sec_per_gpu": 250,
      "pool_tpm": 240000,
      "tenant_share": 0.2,
      "operational_headroom": 0.8,
      "tenant_tpm": 38400,
      "p95_tokens": 3200,
      "tenant_rpm": 12
    }
    ```
ben: wait tenant_tpm 38400 / 3200 -> 12 rpm, seems low vs earlier calc because p95 is large. we should expose both p50 and p95 throttles to be less blunt.
carla: agree. p50 throttle could allow bursty sessions; p95 controls tail protection. implement token-burst bucket + sustained tpm limiter.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-23 (auto) — spike detected in us-west-2; runbook link: https://redwood/s/ops/fleet-spike
maya: I'll run the script against the current pool and post proposed tenant caps in 10m. if we still see >90% after caps, we'll trigger emergency scale or migrate low-priority tenants to dedicated nodes.
ben: ping me when posted, i'll validate with metrics (net-new trace and tail-latency).
carla: thanks. small follow: we should persist per-tenant p95 sizes from eval service to keep this automated.
maya: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
